records.title: Iterative Audit Convergence in LLM-Managed Multi-Agent Systems: A Case Study in Prompt-Engineering Quality Assurance
records.rationale: Measures verification failure in a production seven-lane LLM multi-agent pipeline: 51 consistency defects across nine audit rounds with a seven-category defect taxonomy, non-monotonic convergence, and inter-rater reliability (Cohen's kappa 0.80/0.46). Directly answers RQ3 on how coordination and specification-consistency failure modes are detected and quantified.

records.title: A Multi-Agent LLM Framework for Automated Software Testing
records.rationale: Four-agent test-generation framework evaluated on QuixBugs with a same-model single-agent ablation that attributes the gain to role decomposition rather than the diagnostic agent, plus a 35-point detection-rate gap traced to hallucinated oracle values and signature mismatches. Hits RQ2 (where specialization pays off) and RQ3 (measured verification failure modes) simultaneously.

records.title: Comparing Single-Agent and Multi-Agent Strategies in LLM-Based Title-Abstract Screening
records.rationale: Rare quantified negative result: across five coordination strategies (single-agent, majority voting, recall-focused ensemble, confidence-weighted aggregation, two-stage debate) on a 200-paper gold standard, the single-agent few-shot configuration beat every multi-agent alternative and confidence weighting added no discriminative value. Direct evidence for the RQ2 underperformance condition where coordination overhead outweighs model selection.

records.title: A Comparative Empirical Evaluation of Single-Agent and Multi-Agent LLM Prompting Strategies for Automated Formative Feedback in Education
records.rationale: Controlled four-way comparison over 200 essays with a role-count ablation (zero-shot single, chain-of-thought single, dual-role draft-critique, tri-role draft-critique-revise) showing tri-role wins on quality and hallucination rate while chain-of-thought single-agent reaches near-parity at a fraction of inference cost. The quality-versus-cost parity boundary is exactly the RQ2 condition question, transferable despite the education domain.

records.title: A multi-agent ensemble framework for enhancing task performance using specialized LLM
records.rationale: The recovered text is NOT an abstract: it is Polish-language marketing boilerplate describing the SIGMA-NOT publishing house and its technical journals, with no connection to the paper. Judged from the title alone, a named multi-agent ensemble framework built on specialized LLMs is plausibly relevant to role specialization, so it is retained at supporting pending full-text confirmation of the domain and evaluation.

records.title: A Modular Multi-Agent {LLM} Architecture for Text-to-Diagram Generation and User-Guided Refinement
records.rationale: Published in a software engineering journal and argues directly the RQ2 claim: a pipeline of interpretation, synthesis, validation, and correction agents with deterministic validation loops outperforms monolithic single-pass LLM generation on a design-artifact task. The structured abstract reports no numeric comparison, so full text is needed to establish whether the superiority claim is empirically backed.

records.title: Multi-Agent RAG Framework for Entity Resolution: Advancing Beyond Single-LLM Approaches with Specialized Agent Coordination
records.rationale: Decomposes household entity resolution into four task-specialized LangGraph agents and reports 94.3% accuracy plus a 61% reduction in API calls versus monolithic single-LLM approaches. The efficiency-through-specialization result is a combinable data point on coordination cost even though the domain is record linkage rather than software engineering.

records.title: Benchmarking Multi-Agent LLM and Single Agent LLM Efficiency for Contextual Text Generation
records.rationale: Head-to-head single-agent versus retrieval/reasoning/summarization multi-agent comparison on one model (Gemini-Flash) scored with BLEU, ROUGE, METEOR, and BERTScore, concluding multi-agent wins. Qualifies under the any-domain comparison criterion, but the surface-similarity metrics and absence of reported effect sizes or cost accounting keep it below core.

records.title: Training-Free Agentic AI: Probabilistic Control and Coordination in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
records.rationale: ReDeRef is a named training-free routing controller using Thompson sampling and judge-driven re-routing that cuts token usage 28%, agent calls 17%, and time-to-first-success 19% against random recursive delegation, and degrades gracefully when an agent or judge is impaired. Contributes a reusable coordination-overhead measurement and a robustness-under-degradation protocol rather than a single- versus multi-agent contrast.

records.title: Architectural Transparency in LLM-Based Cognitive Assessment: A Multidimensional TRACE-ED Evaluation of Single-Agent and Multi-Agent Systems
records.rationale: The recovered abstract is a genuine abstract but truncated mid-sentence after the Purpose statement, so only the framing is visible: a multidimensional TRACE-ED transparency evaluation contrasting single-agent and multi-agent architectures beyond accuracy and score agreement. Retained because architecture-level transparency and traceability criteria are a transferable evaluation instrument for RQ3.

records.title: Can AI Close the Grant Funding Gap? A Multi-Agent LLM System for Automated Grant Application Generation with Blind Expert Evaluation, Single-Agent Baseline Comparison, and Design Science Research Framework
records.rationale: The recovered text is a real abstract cut off after one sentence about grant application barriers, so the design must be read from the title: a multi-agent system judged against a single-agent baseline by blinded expert raters within a design science framework. The blinded-expert comparison design is methodologically useful for RQ2 even though grant writing is outside software engineering.

records.title: Safety-aware AI for oncology trial pre-screening: a comparative study of rule-based, single-agent, and multi-agent approaches
records.rationale: The recovered abstract is genuine but truncated after the Background sentence on matching eligibility criteria to heterogeneous records; the title establishes a three-arm comparison of rule-based, single-agent, and multi-agent approaches under safety constraints. The deterministic-baseline arm alongside the single/multi arms is a design worth borrowing for high-stakes reliability comparisons.

records.title: Enhanced Chemical Reasoning Agent: Boosting Trustworthy LLM Performance in Chemistry via Multi-Stage Reasoning and Calibrated Confidence
records.rationale: A single chemistry reasoning agent using multi-stage prompting and confidence calibration evaluated against ChemBench, with no software engineering activity and no single-agent versus multi-agent configuration comparison. Fails both inclusion routes and matches the chemical-domain keyword collision exclusion.

records.title: Evaluation of the Choice of LLM in a Multi-Agent Solution for GUI-Test Generation
records.rationale: PathFinder assigns perception, decision, input-handling, and validation roles for exploratory web GUI testing and sweeps 27 LLM permutations across four e-commerce sites, finding that a uniform LLM across agents gives the best F1 and hypothesizing reduced task-coordination discrepancies as the cause. Empirical software testing evidence that heterogeneous model-per-role pairing introduces coordination cost, answering RQ2 and RQ3.

records.title: Agora: A Drive-Based Framework for Agent Difffferentiation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
records.rationale: Proposes differentiating agents through six continuous drives (boredom, curiosity, stress, anxiety, empathy, service) mapped onto LLM sampling parameters instead of hand-crafted roles or layer stacking; the recovered abstract truncates before any evaluation is described. Offers background framing on how agent specialization can be operationalized, with no software engineering task and no reported results.

records.title: CodeQual-Agent: An Intelligent LLM-Agent Framework for Automated Software Quality Assessment with Explainable Predictions and Real-Time Analysis
records.rationale: Neural-symbolic LLM-agent framework anchoring model reasoning on static-analysis metrics, distilled from GPT-4 and Gemini Pro teachers to a Gemini 2.5 Flash student, with 450ms latency, 150,000 evaluated samples, and deployment evidence of a 14% drop in production defect escape. Supplies an ecologically valid architecture and cost/latency data for the RQ1 verification and sustainability strand, but runs no multi-agent comparison.

records.title: From single-agent to multi-agent: a comprehensive review of LLM-based legal agents
records.rationale: Narrative survey of legal retrieval, question answering, judgment prediction, and text generation that catalogues technical challenges for single-agent and multi-agent designs and proposes future directions in explainability, collaboration efficiency, and ethical governance. Provides background on how the single-to-multi transition is framed in another discipline but reports no comparative evidence and no software engineering tasks.

records.title: Bridging AI and Software Security: A Comparative Vulnerability Assessment of LLM Agent Deployment Paradigms
records.rationale: The recovered abstract is genuine but truncated just as the Function Calling comparison arm is introduced, leaving the remaining paradigms and results unknown. Comparative security evaluation of LLM agent deployment paradigms spanning AI-specific and traditional software vulnerabilities is a usable measurement lens for architecture-level risk, though nothing visible establishes a single- versus multi-agent contrast.

records.title: Review of: "AgentNet: Decentralized Evolutionary Coordination for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems"
records.rationale: Not a primary study: this is a Qeios open peer-review commentary whose recovered text is the reviewer's summary of the AgentNet decentralized coordination framework rather than an abstract of original work. The AgentNet paper itself is the correct record to screen, so this entry is excluded as a secondary pointer to an already-addressable source.

records.title: The Operational Protocol Method: Systematic LLM Specialization Through Collaborative Persona Engineering and Agent Coordination
records.rationale: The recovered abstract is real but truncated after the opening problem statement, which nonetheless names three concrete specialization failure modes: context drift, personality inconsistency, and failure to prioritize curated knowledge. Those named degradation modes plus a protocol-based persona-engineering method are combinable with RQ3's failure-mode taxonomy, though no software engineering evaluation is visible.

records.title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Vehicle Coordination in Smart Cities
records.rationale: The agents are DQN, PPO, and MADDPG reinforcement-learning policies evaluated in SUMO and CARLA traffic simulations, with no language model anywhere in the pipeline. Matches the explicit exclusion for non-LLM reinforcement-learning agents and agent-based simulation.

records.title: Efficient Verification of Multi-Agent Systems Through Parallel
records.rationale: Classical multi-agent model checking: Strategy Computation Tree Logic formulas resolved in parallel on a probe machine via the MC2PM checker to combat state-space explosion. The multi-agent systems here are formal automata, not LLM-based agents, so the record is a terminology collision with no language-model content.
